name: VCC 1287 (Hubble)
blurb: VCC 1287, an ultra-diffuse galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, seen by Hubble.
label: vcc1287-hubble
story: An ultra-diffuse galaxy, as wide as a giant but as faint as a dwarf, adrift in the Virgo Cluster. By following its globular clusters, astronomers weighed it and found an overmassive dark halo around its thin veil of stars.

claims.text: VCC 1287 is an ultra-diffuse galaxy in the Virgo Cluster
Ultra-diffuse galaxies have the sizes of giant galaxies but the luminosities of dwarfs
VCC 1287's mass was measured using its globular clusters, revealing an overmassive dark halo
VCC 1287 belongs to the Virgo Cluster and has a globular cluster system
VCC 1287 is a low surface brightness galaxy targeted by program 17528 on Virgo Cluster UDGs
